chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Buraid ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the redness disappears from this side — meaning from the east — then the sun has set from the east of the earth and its west.

key_terms.الْجَانِبِ: Side or direction — here referring to the eastern horizon as opposed to the west where the sun physically sets
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness or red glow in the sky — specifically the redness that appears in the eastern horizon as a residual effect of sunset
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: The east, the direction of sunrise — the criterion for Maghrib prayer time per this hadith
key_terms.غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun has set — understood in its comprehensive sense as setting from both the east and west of the earth simultaneously

ai.seo_question: When does the Maghrib prayer time begin according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) provides a practical criterion for determining when the Maghrib prayer time begins: when the red glow of sunset disappears from the eastern horizon. This teaching addresses a natural observation that ancient scholars debated — the appearance of redness in the east after sunset — and clarifies that its disappearance, not merely the sun's descent below the western horizon, marks the true beginning of the Maghrib time. This ruling reflects the Imami jurisprudential position, distinguishing it from those who hold the Maghrib time begins at the mere disappearance of the sun's disc.
